case.background: Monochromatic light passes through two narrow parallel slits and forms alternating bright and dark bands on a screen. Vary only the listed controls and infer a predictive law for adjacent bright-fringe spacing.
initial_observations: Blocking either slit removes the regular band pattern.
Changing the geometry shifts the bright bands, but the dependence is not given.

controls.description: Wavelength of the monochromatic incident light.
controls.name: wavelength_nm

controls.description: Distance from the slits to the observation screen.
controls.name: screen_distance_m

controls.description: Center-to-center separation of the two narrow slits.
controls.name: slit_separation_mm

instruments.description: A monochromatic source coherently illuminates two narrow parallel slits, with a movable screen and a scale for adjacent bright fringes.
instruments.name: double_slit_screen

notes: Both narrow parallel slits are mutually coherently illuminated.
Only central paraxial fringes are measured, with screen distance much larger than slit separation.
The screen remains normal to the incident beam.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'double_slit_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_spacing_mm, wavelength_exponent, screen_distance_exponent, slit_separation_exponent. Candidate law: spacing = reference_spacing_mm * (wavelength_nm / 550 nm)^wavelength_exponent * (screen_distance_m / 1 m)^screen_distance_exponent * (slit_separation_mm / 0.50 mm)^slit_separation_exponent.

readouts.description: Mean separation between adjacent bright fringes.
readouts.name: fringe_spacing_mm

case.title: Identify the double-slit fringe response
